text:
maya (eng-platform): quick sync: UX asks for a per-route toggle on the Cost dashboard: 'Show costs by model SKU' vs 'Show costs by route'. the tricky bit is amortized prefetch savings and shared prefetches. thoughts?

eli (product-analytics): users want both. ops teams care about model SKU economics, product teams care about route-level unit cost. toggle should persist per-user. :white_check_mark:

toni (eng-runtime): technically we have two orthogonal aggregates: 1) attribute savings at model SKU level by dividing shared prefetch according to observed hit contributions; 2) attribute at route level by proportional token usage. either needs lineage data from the prefetch table.

naveen (eng-platform): that's doable but important to call out sampling bias. at 1% sample rate our hit-rate estimation can be noisy, especially for low-traffic routes. we should surface a sample_rate and confidence band in the UI.

aldo (billing): for invoices we prefer deterministic daily aggregates. recommend we export both views in billing CSV: sku_aggregate_daily and route_aggregate_daily. that solves disputes.

maya (eng-platform): UX question: when a route is in canary and traffic splits across model variants, do we show combined cost or break out canary vs stable? eli: product asked for explicit canary delta.

eli (product-analytics): break it out. a small column: canary_percent and canary_cost_delta. users should see "canary cost vs baseline". also show an anchor to the rollout config.

toni (eng-runtime): we emit model_variant per invocation in traces. for dashboards we only keep aggregates. plan: when a rollout is active, compute delta = (weighted_cost(canary_variants) - weighted_cost(baseline_variant)) and expose as separate fields.

naveen (eng-platform): edgecase: quota-triggered reroute. if request is rerouted because of quota to a cheaper variant, the route's effective cost drops but we'd be hiding that it's quota-driven. propose a small enum reason: reason in ["normal","quota_reroute","fallback_region","overload_shrink"] and visible in the drilldown.

aldo (billing): add to CSV too. reason column helps with chargeback investigations.

ui-bot: mock uploaded -> https://figma.com/s/route-cost-toggle (view-only).

maya (eng-platform): telemetry question: what metric do we show for cache savings? bytes_saved vs tokens_saved vs $saved. which is clearest?

eli (product-analytics): show percent saved + an example invocation equivalence like "~3.4 invocations worth". dollars fluctuate by sku and not great for normalized comparison. dollars should be toggleable for billing users.

toni (eng-runtime): internal note: our ingest currently records cache_hit_bytes and request_token_count. dollars_saved needs model_sku_price * effective_tokens_avoided which requires joining pricing table. joining at query time is expensive. prefer precompute nightly.

naveen (eng-platform): agree. nightly precompute job: per-tenant, per-route, per-sku daily rows with fields [date, tenant_id, route_id, sku, token_burn, tokens_saved_est, shared_prefetch_pct, reason, sample_rate, derived_from_sample]. expose via /v1/costs/summary?group=route&range=1d.

aldo (billing): ensure the derived flag is included. if derived_from_sample=true we should apply a correction factor and include it in the CSV as "est_correction_applied". auditors will ask.

eli (product-analytics): for low-volume routes (<100 req/day) hide per-invocation equivalence and show only aggregated percent + note "low volume". avoids wild ratios.

maya (eng-platform): rollout plan: 1) API contract PR for /v1/costs/summary with new fields. 2) nightly job for daily aggregates. 3) UI toggle + drilldown panel. 4) CSV export columns and docs. target: staging canary next sprint.

toni (eng-runtime): performance note: UI should fetch the summary blob with the dashboard payload to avoid extra roundtrips. also cache the blob for 30s to avoid spikes when many users open panel.

naveen (eng-platform): I'll add a small rate-limit on the CSV generation endpoint and require admin permission for full tenant exports. partial exports allowed for users.

aldo (billing): one more ask 1) tag-based rollups: customers use tags to map routes to products. please include the primary_tag in the aggregated rows so finance can roll up by product.

maya (eng-platform): good call. we'll add primary_tag to the nightly aggregates.

eli (product-analytics): sample query for precompute (draft):
```sql
-- approximate tokens saved per tenant-route-sku
select
  tenant_id,
  route_id,
  sku,
  date_trunc('day', ts) as day,
  sum(token_count) as token_burn,
  sum(case when cache_hit then token_count else 0 end) as tokens_saved_sample,
  count(*) as sampled_invocations
from request_samples
where ts >= now() - interval '7 days'
group by tenant_id, route_id, sku, day;
```

toni (eng-runtime): looks fine as a start. we'll need to join prefetch_lineage to compute shared_prefetch_pct. I'll add a join in my PR.

ui-bot: deploy queued -> cost-summary-precompute v0.1 to staging. initiated by @maya. :rocket:

naveen (eng-platform): I'll own the API PR. assigning reviewers: @toni, @eli, @aldo.

aldo (billing): please cc me when staging data is ready so I can validate numbers.

maya (eng-platform): thanks all. I'll create a short RFC with screenshots and link this thread. if you have specific example tenants/routes we should test with, drop them here.

eli (product-analytics): dropping two test tenants: tenant-alpha, tenant-beta. both have shared-prefetch patterns.

maya (eng-platform): perfect. that's it for now.
